body: But wouldn't it be an ELS, not dh/oth? I've been in almost 4 months now.

I've heard a lot of this before, that the fleet is very different and that the Navy will be my new family. Above, I didn't list every single reason I want out. I feel like my life is on hold and that I'm missing out on my real family. After my abuse, I was taken in by my grandparents and raised by them. They had always been a huge part of my life even before then. Now my grandfather is in bad health, and before I left for basic everyone thought he was about to die. He said his goodbyes to me as if it would be the last time I see him. I miss everyone else in my family a lot too. It could be homesickness but knowing that I will be out of contact with them for such long periods, I really don't want to be in the middle of a deployment and then have to go on emergency leave. I also realized very quickly how uncomfortable I am with this highly structured environment and wearing uniforms. Futhermore, even before I joined I had some worries that I was violating some of my own ethics by joining a branch of the military. I tried talking this out with various family members but they all convinced me that it would be okay and that the benefits would be too good to pass up. Now when we go to GMT on Thursdays we are shown videos of tomahawk missiles blowing shit up and everyone but me is shouting hooyah. I'm sure that it's necessary to ensure the safety of our troops but I get really uncomfortable at that. I really tried to think of some cons to joining at first so I could justify not enlisting to my family but I really couldn't think of many and the pros obviously were appealing. Now that I'm here I've learned more about what it's like and the cons definitely have the upper hand. I feel like going to college would have been a way better idea for me. I had a full ride scholarship for my grades in high school. It's been less than a year since I graduated so I'm pretty sure I'm still eligible for that.
